ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The image shows a transition-state style drawing with curved arrows that are to be disregarded. On the left is a Ph–CO–CO–Ph fragment: two phenyl groups attached to two adjacent carbonyl carbons, with each carbonyl carbon double-bonded to oxygen and the two carbonyl carbons bonded to each other. On the right is a sulfur/carbanion ester-containing fragment: a negatively charged central carbon connected to a CO2Et group and to sulfur, and the sulfur connected through a carbon chain to another CO2Et group. Reasoning: Following the assigned counting method and excluding bonds to hydrogen, count bonds component by component. For the left Ph–CO–CO–Ph portion, each phenyl group contributes 6 aromatic ring bonds plus 1 bond from the phenyl ring to the carbonyl carbon, so two phenyl groups contribute 14 bonds. Add the 2 C=O bonds and the central C–C bond between the two carbonyl carbons, giving 14 + 2 + 1 = 17 bonds. For the right sulfur/carbanion ester portion, each CO2Et substituent contributes 5 non-H bonds: its attachment bond, the carbonyl bond, the C–O bond, the O–ethyl bond, and the ethyl C–C bond. Two such CO2Et groups give 10 bonds. Add the central C–S bond and the S–CH2 bond, giving 10 + 2 = 12 bonds. Total = 17 + 12 = 29.

method.method_draft: Construct the heavy-atom adjacency graph and count edges once. The left dicarbonyl graph has two phenyl rings with 6 ring edges each, two phenyl–carbonyl edges, two carbonyl C=O edges, and one carbonyl-carbonyl edge: 12 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 17. The right graph has an upper ester branch attached to the carbanion with edges C−C(=O), C=O, C−O, O−Et, and the Et C−C edge = 5; a lower ester branch reached through C−S−CH2 has S−C and S−CH2 edges plus CH2−C(=O), C=O, C−O, O−Et, and Et C−C edges = 7. The right component therefore has 12 edges, and the whole drawing has 17 + 12 = 29 non-hydrogen bonds.
